newsitem.title: USA: Mass Water Resources panel wants to cut cap budget.
newsitem.headline: Mass Water Resources panel wants to cut cap budget.

text.p: The Massachusetts Water Resources Advisory Board on Thursday recommended slicing $147 million off the agency's proposed capital budget for fiscal 1998 to 2000, saying it wanted to restrain rate increases.

Further, the advisory board, which predicted its recommendations would be adopted, sought to reschedule $76 million of spending that was planned for fiscal 1998, a step that would save about $3 million in debt service.

"We anticipate that the MWRA will adopt our proposed reductions in order to reduce borrowing and control future rate increases," stated Andrew Pappastergion, chairman of the MWRA Advisory Board, in prepared remarks.
The panel made a number of specific recommendations in its analysis of the proposed budget, which totals $2.9 billion.

The list includes: $37.4 million in revised start dates for construction. Another $19.7 million of cuts was due to modifications in emergency funds, with $13.4 million stemming from postponing the priority of some projects. The smallest item, $5.8 million, reflected some lower contract awards.
